utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see the Prosecution is in hibernation. Yes, Ms. Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. The Prosecution wants to call next witness. It is a protected witness, MM-018. He will testify in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Let the witness come through. May the Chamber please move into closed session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Whiting, you are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I didn't mean to take over, but Ms. Richterova asked me to handle the next matter because she would like to be excused so that -- and she asked me to ask Your Honours if she may be excused from the further proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I see she always asks you to ask the Chamber if she may be excused. I wonder how much she -- she pays you for that representation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Not enough, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ms. Richterova, you are excused.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't have another witness for today, for this week. We estimated that the witnesses for this week would take us to the end. We fell a little bit short, so our next witness will not be available until Monday, I'm afraid. We do have two small housekeeping matters to address with the Court, if we could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The first is with respect, once again, to the books, the three books. If you'll recall, Your Honour, the Court gave us with respect to one of those three books, Exhibit 238, until today to make our selection. We have done that. The selection is completed. The translation has been completed. It was no small effort, I can say, and I'd like to thank the interpreters in our office who worked very hard to get that done. The only thing that has to be done is it has not yet been uploaded into e-court. That I think can be accomplished today, both the B/C/S pages that were selected and their accompanying translation. What I think I would ask is if the Court could ask the registrar to assign an exhibit number once it has been uploaded to e-court. Then what we can do is simply deal directly with the registrar on that, get it uploaded to e-court, tell the registrar what it is in e-court and the number can then just be assigned and the process will be done with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Registrar, will you please assign an exhibit number to that exhibit once it has been uploaded in e-court and do that outside court?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I move to the next housekeeping topic which is a separate matter, I do wonder if the Defence might be in a position to address whether it has made its selections with respect to these three books. Perhaps it's been done. I'm not clear on whether it's been done and whether they have been assigned exhibit numbers and where we stand on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, do you have anything to tell us about your side of the story on the three exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We've obeyed by your instructions. At this moment, I don't know whether we have those exhibits. Could we please leave this until Monday as a technical issue that may be resolved at that time, since my learned friend Mr. Sekulic is not with us today and he is much more familiar with that. But undoubtedly we followed your instruction on all three books.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Registry advises me that it has been done. What remains is to be uploaded on to e-court. So you more or less are at the same level as the Prosecution on that one. Thank you very much. Mr. Whiting, the next point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next point requires us to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you go into private session, can I deal with a point -- the housekeeping point that doesn't need private session? Just to remind the parties, or to let the parties know, rather, that a Scheduling Order has been filed scheduling the case after the close of the Prosecution case. I'm just mentioning this so that you may try -- you may try to access that today and familiarise yourselves with that Scheduling Order because we are going to try to keep very strictly to that Scheduling Order for the conduct of the case after the close of the Prosecution case. So the sooner you get your hands on it, the better. Okay. May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Nothing to be dealt with now? Do you have anything outstanding, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I do not, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Court adjourned then. We will reconvene on Monday, I guess it's going to be at 2.00 -- quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In which courtroom? This is Courtroom III. How about next week, is it Courtroom II or Courtroom III?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's going to be in Courtroom II. We were just here today because, I suppose, because something is being done to Courtroom II. So it's going to be Courtroom II, quarter past 2.00, on Monday. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 12th day of June, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.50 a.m.,
